chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from 'Isa ibn Hamzah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever wears a turban and does not pass the turban under his chin, then if a pain for which there is no remedy afflicts him, let him blame none but himself."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no harm in a person performing salat (prayer) in a single waist-wrapper, using part of it as a lower wrap and the other part as an upper covering.

key_terms.يَأْتَزِرُ: to wrap oneself with it around the lower body
key_terms.يَرْتَدِي: to drape oneself with it over the upper body

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in a single garment, and what is the ruling on wearing the turban without passing it under the chin?
ai.summary: This report mentions an instruction concerning the manner of wearing the turban, warning against leaving off passing it beneath the chin. It also includes a juristic note from al-Shaykh that it is permissible for a person to perform salat (prayer) in a single garment, wrapping part of it around the lower body and draping the rest over the upper body.
